method: A two-way Wilkinson divider splits one input into two outputs through a quarter-wave line in each arm, with a resistor bridging the two outputs. With K squared equal to the port 3 power divided by the port 2 power, the arm to port 2 is Z0 times the square root of K times (1 + K squared), the arm to port 3 is Z0 times the square root of (1 + K squared) divided by K cubed, and the isolation resistor is Z0 times (K + 1/K). At K = 1, an equal split, both arms become Z0 times the square root of two and the resistor becomes twice Z0, which is the familiar 1.414 x Z0 arm and 2 x Z0 resistor rule. In fifty ohms at 2.45 GHz the equal-split arms are 70.711 ohms and the resistor is 100.0 ohms; a two-to-one split with two thirds of the power at port 2 gives arms of 51.494 ohms and 102.988 ohms with a 106.066 ohm resistor, so each arm must be built from its own impedance. Each arm is 90 degrees of electrical length at the design frequency, so its physical length is a quarter of the guided wavelength, which is the velocity factor times the free-space wavelength; at 2.45 GHz on 0.66 velocity factor the guided wavelength is 80.760 mm and each arm is 20.190 mm. The page also reports the output level at each port as 10 log10 of its power share, -3.01 dB each for an equal split. The system impedance is limited to 5 to 1000 ohms, the frequency to 0.1 to 40000 MHz, the velocity factor to 0.3 to 1 and the port 2 share to 5 to 95 percent; text, negative values, values outside those ranges and an empty field are refused with the field named. The model is an ideal lossless quarter-wave network with a matched source and matched loads: dispersion, junction capacitance, resistor tolerance, line loss and the layout's distance from the ground plane are not modelled, and match and isolation degrade away from the design frequency. The page stores, uploads and transmits nothing.

sources.title: Microwaves101, Wilkinson Power Splitters: the arms are quarter-wave transformers of 1.414 x Z0 and a 2 x Z0 resistor isolates the two outputs.
Wilkinson power divider, unequal-split design equations Z02 = Z0 sqrt(K(1+K^2)), Z03 = Z0 sqrt((1+K^2)/K^3) and R = Z0 (K + 1/K), after Pozar, Microwave Engineering.
